why: The scan test and the rule are cheap, but each of some 40 deletions depends on the executor reading an action it was only named, confirming refresh() runs on the success path (sometimes inside a storeAction handler, sometimes across four or five actions bound to one prop) and that the client call sits on that same path. A misread deletes a needed router.refresh(); the scan test only counts calls and lowers its own baseline, and the signed-in specs cover a minority of these screens.
harm_if_wrong: A save that succeeds but leaves the screen showing the old figure (stock adjustments, supplier orders, two-step removal, imports), so an owner repeats an adjustment or thinks a change failed.
make_it_cheaper: Record in the brief, for every line to delete, the file:line of the refresh() in each action it can call (as done for locations/actions.ts), and move the unresolved and mixed lines to a later step, so the executor only deletes listed lines.
brief_problems: Line numbers are a snapshot; most hold today (inventory-table 139/151, discount-editor 127, pack-pictures 59/111/131/178, two-step-panel 195/262), but the rule leaves actions that only call updateTag/refreshTag or revalidatePath (not refresh()) undecided.
'3 more by hand' in the decision row is not defined anywhere in the brief.
